title: InformationCommons
description: An edited volume examining open standards and cognitive security for structuring the information commons. The book addresses how information ecosystems can be designed to promote trust, transparency...
abstract: An edited volume examining open standards and cognitive security for structuring the information commons. The book addresses how information ecosystems can be designed to promote trust, transparency, and collective sensemaking through open standards, decentralized governance, and cognitive security principles.

methods.name: Edited volume of eleven chapters from the VIE program's first year
methods.description: Collects all work submitted and approved through the UW APL VIE program during Phase 1 of NSF Convergence Accelerator Track F (2021), ordered by submission.
methods.evidence: This volume presents all work submitted and approved for publication through the VIE program in the initial year of the project (during Phase 1 of the NSF Convergence Accelerator Track F in 2021), in order of their submission and approval.

methods.name: Catechism-based project management across participating teams
methods.description: The program coordinated contributing teams using question-based, versionable project documentation adapted from DARPA practice.
methods.evidence: The program made use of the recently formalized methodology known as “catechism-based project management”, which applies question-based, versionable project documentation

methods.name: Framing the information environment as a proto-market needing exchange protocols
methods.description: The program treated online information as a proto-market and aimed to lay foundations for Verified Information Exchange environments (VIEs).
methods.evidence: framed the global information environment as a proto-market for information in need of exchange protocols and local standards setting in order to de-risk, reduce volatility, and increase trust in digital information transactions.

methods.name: Expert discussions and interviews feeding market-maturity and design chapters
methods.description: Chapters such as 'Elements Related to Maturity of Function in Markets' and 'TrustFinder' synthesize program discussions and interviews with experts.
methods.evidence: The VIE Program’s discussions and interviews with experts on mechanism design and economics featured a recurring theme of “maturity of function” in markets.

key_findings: The editors suggest focusing on shared context and meaning as a key element of co-managing the information commons, broadening attention from data security to context sharing.
The editors argue that declining trust online, viewed as a market with growing pains, is a new instance of an old problem traditionally solved by shared exchange protocols and local rule-setting.
Chapter I (Cordes et al.) proposes Narrative Information Management as a unifying term and framework for the features and challenges of collective sensemaking.
Chapter V applies Active Inference to model conflict as multiscale processes of communication, trust, and relationship management among agents.
Chapter XI presents a design document for TrustFinder, a sociotechnical system for clearinghouses of granular, modular information products.
key_findings_evidence: Our suggestion, explored in this volume, is that focus be placed on shared context and meaning as a key element of co- management of the information commons
